valuation.method: Forward non-GAAP EPS x justified P/E, with FY2027 EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance is $22.90-$23.70 (midpoint $23.30) from the Q3 2026 release; FY2027 EPS of about $23.5-$23.7 is a third-party consensus range and is not a company figure. Listing is the USD Nasdaq share, so no FX conversion is needed. Bear, base and bull EPS are model assumptions, not company guidance. Sensitivities use the same EPS base.

bear.driver: Prolia biosimilar erosion (Q3 sales -45%) and Enbrel net price cut (-14% from Medicare Part D pricing) outrun new launches; MariTide launch slips and the multiple de-rates

base.driver: Imdelltra, Repatha and Tezspire growth roughly offsets Prolia and Enbrel erosion; no material MariTide revenue in 2027; buybacks capped at $3.0bn

bull.driver: MariTide Phase 3 progress and earlier launch plus Imdelltra label expansion lift EPS; the multiple re-rates on a visible growth pipeline

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS of $23.50 the close of $465.67 implies 19.8x; at the 19x base multiple the close is about 4% above the base target. The sample mean of the seven analyst targets above (about $404) implies 17.2x base EPS, and the 29-analyst Yahoo Finance mean of $432.84 implies 18.4x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $23.50 (about 5.0 pp of the close). A $1.00 change in FY2027 EPS at 19x moves the base target by $19.00 (about 4.1 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Gross-to-net and volume trend for Prolia and Enbrel, together with FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance. A guide below about $23 would weaken the base case; MariTide Phase 3 timing and any 2027 launch plan would support it.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance, expected around early February 2027 (date not confirmed in the sources reviewed).

analyst_notes: Partial panel of seven named-firm views, all dated in 2026. Since the Q3 release on 3 Nov 2026, Freedom Broker moved to Hold (6 Nov) and lifted its target to $470 from $450. The August post-Q2 wave (Morgan Stanley, Truist, Scotiabank, TD Cowen, RBC) raised targets to $351-$452, but ratings are split: three Buy (Scotiabank, TD Cowen, RBC) against four Hold-equivalents (Freedom, Guggenheim, Morgan Stanley, Truist). The sample target median of $400 sits about 14% below the close and about $46.50 below our $446.50 base. Bridging that gap takes about 2 turns of P/E at base EPS, or about $2.50 of FY2027 EPS at 19x; the sources do not show which assumption the panel uses. Most targets are older than the Q3 release, and the sample has no 12-month horizon disclosure, so no event enters the weighted target. Yahoo Finance aggregate (29 analysts, mean $432.84, consensus Hold) is shown for context only and is not used in the valuation.
